SM18L-A1.free_elimination: -12 is the printed 12 with a sign flipped (echo); -3/-2 are an adjacent pair but nothing structural picks between them
SM18L-A1.note: Borderline hard. 'At least one solution' is a real decision point (same slope forces coincide-or-nothing), but the ratio-of-coefficients procedure is a well-drilled template. Keep.

SM18L-A2.free_elimination: 48 falls by range: y<=-x+27 with y>=0 caps x at the printed 27, and 48 is also the sum of the two printed constants (closure). 7 and 15 need the intersection.
SM18L-A2.note: Routine: find all four vertices (0,0),(7,0),(12,15),(0,27) and read off max x. No decision point beyond sketching. Sound item, medium.

SM18L-A3.free_elimination: 12 = 4*3 and 45 = 15*3 are products of printed numbers (closure); a savvy student strikes at least 12 as the bare input change. 41 is the odd non-multiple-of-3 and falls once the student sees the answer must be slope*12.
SM18L-A3.note: Bypass: f(x)=3x+5, g(t)=12t+2, difference 36 in three lines. Correct and clean; medium on the hard route.

SM18L-A4.free_elimination: 12 = 2*6 (printed echo) and 21 = 3*5+6 (closure of printed numbers). 7 survives as an endpoint decoy.
SM18L-A4.note: The midpoint-is-irrelevant insight is nice, but the routine path (midpoint gives c=15, interval [3,7], length 4) is short and needs no insight. Medium.

SM18L-A5.free_elimination: 148 = 180-32 falls by range with no arithmetic: a 10-page job must cost less than the printed 50-page $32, so the difference must exceed 148. Others need the fee.
SM18L-A5.note: Cap of $180 is attainable (p=420). Two constraints in two variables is a mild decision point; the work is routine. Medium.

SM18L-A6.free_elimination: 21 = 3 * 7, i.e. the printed 3k evaluated at another OPTION. A distractor built from the key plus a printed number points at the key. 9 and 13 are 5+4 and 5+8 (printed 5 plus printed |coefficients|), also closure.
SM18L-A6.note: Routine: collect terms, match the y-coefficient. c=10.5 non-integer is fine since c is not asked. The 21-tell is the worst structural issue in the batch: replace 21 with a value not derivable as 3*(option).

SM18L-A7.free_elimination: 4 is struck for free: it zeroes the printed denominator (x-4). That leaves three.
SM18L-A7.note: OFF BLUEPRINT: clearing denominators yields a quadratic; rational equations with extraneous roots are Advanced Math (nonlinear equations in one variable), not Algebra. Also, the extraneous candidate is printed as an option that a student can dismiss by inspection, so the 'extraneous' decision point is never exercised. Drop from an Algebra batch.

SM18L-B1.free_elimination: 186 - 126 = 60 = the printed fixed fee. The pair tells the student one of them 'forgot the fee', and the fee-inclusive one is the key. 74 is the raw 40-as-square-feet echo. Key identifiable without converting units.
SM18L-B1.note: One unit conversion and one linear evaluation. This is a module-1 medium at most. DROP for difficulty; the fee-pair tell compounds it.

SM18L-B2.free_elimination: Three of four options are multiples of 7 (7, 21, 49) and 49 = 7^2 is a square of an option. Odd-one-out strikes 29; 49 reads as an intermediate squared; 7 reads as the intermediate itself. The key is the remaining multiple of 7. No arithmetic needed.
SM18L-B2.note: Classic symmetric-system item; the add/subtract insight is bypassable by solving (x,y)=(5,2) directly in four lines. Option set leaks the key by multiples-of-7 structure. Hold pending distractor rewrite (e.g. replace 49 and 29 with non-multiples that are not squares of options).

SM18L-B3.free_elimination: Sign: target slope 2/3 is positive. For k=17 the first point sits at (17,34) above y=14 and to the left of 47, so the slope is negative; for k=-8 the first point (-8,-16) is to the RIGHT of 3k-4=-28 and below 14, again negative. Both fall by sign reasoning with almost no arithmetic. 3 needs the computation.
SM18L-B3.note: Routine parallel-slope equation in k. Correct, medium.

SM18L-B4.free_elimination: 420 = 105/0.25 is the usage if EVERY kWh were at the top rate, so it is a strict lower bound on usage; falls by magnitude with one division. The three third-tier options need the tier boundary.
SM18L-B4.note: Tier identification ($78 at 500 kWh) is the one decision point; after that it is one subtraction and one division. Standard tiered-pricing medium. Keep.

SM18L-B5.free_elimination: None structural. 19 = 24-5 and 10 do not echo printed numbers; the set does not leak.
SM18L-B5.note: Recounted: x>8 gives 9..12 (4); x<-3 gives -12..-4 (9); total 13, confirmed by brute force. Genuinely hard (sign case split) but a rational inequality is NOT an SAT Algebra construct and not on the Digital SAT at all. DROP for blueprint, as the prior reviewer said.

SM18L-B6.free_elimination: None structural; 6 and 8 are divisor counts of printed 18 and derived 30, not echoes of the stem.
SM18L-B6.note: Recounted: x = 4 + 30/(k-3); positive divisors give 8, negative divisors -10,-15,-30 give x=1,2,3; total 11, confirmed by brute force over k in [-2000,2000]. Hard and clean, but divisor counting is number theory, not SAT Algebra. DROP for blueprint.

SM18L-B7.free_elimination: 11 = 3 + 8: printed coefficient 3 plus an OPTION, the same closure tell as A6's 21 = 3*7. Points at 8. The -2/2 sign pair is the standard 'one of these is the key' bait and here misleads, which is fine.
SM18L-B7.note: Substitute y=7-x, get (2,5), plug in. Two steps, no decision point; 'exactly one solution' is decorative. DROP for difficulty (or demote to easy/medium).
